title: AlphaGenome 2: Teaching AI to read the entire human genome
summary_raw: 98% of human DNA doesn't build proteins—it controls how our cells work, and holds vital clues to why diseases happen and why 90% of new drugs fail in clinical trials. Understanding the genome at the molecular level is the key to deciphering the blueprint of human life. In this episode, Professor Hannah Fry speaks with Google DeepMind's Žiga Avsec and Adam Gayoso about AlphaGenome, the AlphaGenome Atlas, and AlphaGenome 2—exploring how AI reads non-coding DNA down to single-cell resolution to pinpoint disease-causing mutations and help researchers solve medical mysteries. title: Gemini Decisions API
summary_raw: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. OpenAI can handle text and images. Gemini Decision 1 is fully multi-model: it covers text, images, audio

title: llm 0.37.2
summary_raw: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . Tags: projects , security , llm , releases

title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2
summary_raw: Google Deepmind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that analyzes genetic variants for individual cell types rather than across bulk tissue. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. The model is available for noncommercial research through an API and is set to be integrated into Google's agentic platform Antigravity. A new regulator would enforce independent model audits and impose steep penalties for violations. title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
summary_raw: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks, a process that typically takes years. AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines of proof code and flagged only about one percent for human review. Deepmind plans to extend the method to critical infrastructure like power grids and medical devices.
